description: Composite TEM figure of eight dark-field (DF) images arranged in two rows of four, every panel carrying a 50 nm scale bar and an inset selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern in its upper-right corner. The top row (a–d) is the 0.02Nb steel and the bottom row (e–h) the 0.04Nb steel; within each row the four panels are labelled as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h. The DF images show bright nano-scale κ-carbide particles dispersed in a darker austenite matrix; particle density and brightness increase progressively with aging temperature from the sparse as-cast state to the heavily populated 823 K/3 h state in both rows. Each SAED inset is a zone-axis pattern annotated [100]<sub>γ</sub>//[100]<sub>κ</sub>, with white fundamental reflections marked 020 and 002 and yellow superlattice reflections marked 011, 010 and 001, evidencing an ordered κ-carbide/austenite orientation relationship. Comparing rows, the 0.04Nb images show no obviously higher particle density than the 0.02Nb images at the same aging condition. No numeric particle sizes or volume fractions are printed on any panel; the figure is qualitative, with the cited quantitative values reported elsewhere.

subfigures.description: TEM dark-field image of the as-cast 0.02Nb steel: a dark matrix with a sparse dispersion of faint bright nano-scale κ-carbide particles, 50 nm scale bar. Inset SAED pattern with zone axis [100]γ//[100]κ showing white fundamental reflections 020 and 002 and yellow superlattice reflections 011, 010 and 001.
TEM dark-field image of the 0.02Nb steel after 723 K/3 h aging: markedly denser bright nano-scale particles than (a), 50 nm scale bar, with the same [100]γ//[100]κ SAED inset.

TEM dark-field image of the 0.02Nb steel after 773 K/3 h aging: dense, slightly coarser bright κ-carbide particles; the scale-bar text renders as '50 μm' although the magnitude matches the 50 nm bars of the other panels, and the SAED inset is labelled [100]γ//[100]κ.

TEM dark-field image of the 0.02Nb steel after 823 K/3 h aging: the most densely and brightly populated of the top row, with fine particles covering the field of view, 50 nm scale bar and [100]γ//[100]κ SAED inset.

TEM dark-field image of the as-cast 0.04Nb steel: dark matrix with few, faint bright precipitates, 50 nm scale bar; SAED inset labelled [100]γ//[100]κ with the same 011/010/001 superlattice and 020/002 fundamental reflections.
TEM dark-field image of the 0.04Nb steel after 723 K/3 h aging: numerous bright nano-scale particles dispersed in the matrix, clearly more than in (e), 50 nm scale bar, [100]γ//[100]κ SAED inset.
TEM dark-field image of the 0.04Nb steel after 773 K/3 h aging: dense bright particle population; 50 nm scale bar and [100]γ//[100]κ SAED inset.
TEM dark-field image of the 0.04Nb steel after 823 K/3 h aging: highly populated bright particle field similar in appearance to (d); 50 nm scale bar and [100]γ//[100]κ SAED inset.

observations.observation: Figure 6 is a two-row by four-column composite of TEM dark-field (DF) micrographs, each panel containing an inset SAED pattern and a 50 nm scale bar.
The top row (a-d) is labelled as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h, and the bottom row (e-h) carries the identical four condition labels.
All eight SAED insets are indexed on the zone axis [100]γ//[100]κ, with white fundamental reflections marked 020 and 002 and yellow superlattice reflections marked 011, 010 and 001.

In every panel the κ-carbides appear as bright nano-scale particles dispersed in a darker austenite matrix, and the particle density and brightness increase progressively from the as-cast state to 823 K/3 h in both rows.

The 0.04Nb row (e-h) does not visibly show a higher particle density than the 0.02Nb row (a-d) at the same aging condition; the two rows look comparable, which is consistent with the cited statement that 0.04Nb has the smaller κ-carbide content.
No numeric κ-carbide size, volume fraction or counting statistics are printed anywhere in the panels; all values in this figure are qualitative image contrast.
TEM characterization was performed on intragranular κ-carbides in the a-d) 0.02Nb and e-h) 0.04Nb steels.

The caption states the panels include the SAED patterns corresponding to the dark-field images, and the citing text states that the coherent relationship between the ordered κ-carbides and austenite is demonstrated by the SAED analysis.
The citing text states that a large amount of nano-scale κ-carbides is dispersed in the austenite, which matches the dense bright particle fields seen in the aged panels.

The citing text states the measured content and size of κ-carbides are shown in Figure 7, not in this figure: after 823 K aging the volume fraction of κ-carbides in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels increases from 3.3 and 1.6 vol% in the as-cast state to 27.8 and 26.7 vol%, respectively.
The citing text states the average κ-carbide size in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels increases from 2.0 and 1.9 nm to 7.8 and 6.4 nm, respectively, after aging at 823 K.

The citing text states that κ-carbides in the 0.04Nb steels consistently have a smaller content and size than those in the 0.02Nb steels, and that the increased Nb content decreases both the content and size of κ-carbides (Figures 6 and 7).

The citing text states that a portion of the TEM DF image was enlarged and only clear areas were selected to count κ-carbide size in ImageJ, with multiple regions averaged per sample; the panels themselves contain no such counted values.
The citing text states the uniform distribution of κ-carbides and Nb in the austenite (Figures 6 and 15) supports the inference that Nb atoms are present within the κ-carbides.

κ-carbide volume fraction (vol%) — reported in citing text, not printed on the panels
